record.original_question: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. If |P| = k, and two construction lines have the same slope exactly when they are parallel, how many distinct slopes or directions can the construction lines of such an arrangement determine as a function of k?

evidence.quote: How many distinct slopes, or directions, are defined by construction lines that k points determine?
In this paper, empirical evidence is reported for small numbers of k offering partial answers to the three problems above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define an arrangement in the Euclidean plane to be a pair (L, P), where L is a finite set of straight lines and P is a finite set of points satisfying:
(i) every point of P is the intersection of at least two lines of L;
(ii) any two non-parallel lines of L meet in a unique point that belongs to P.
Two lines of L are declared to have the same slope (direction) if and only if they are parallel.

For an integer k ≥ 2, let S(k) denote the set of all integers d such that there exists an arrangement (L, P) with |P| = k in which the lines of L realize exactly d distinct slopes.

Determine S(k) as a function of k; in particular, determine the minimum and the maximum number of distinct slopes that the lines of such an arrangement can realize when |P| = k, and characterize all values of d ∈ S(k) that are attained between these extremes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of several open questions about point-line arrangements ("arrangements containing shapes"), with only empirical/partial data reported for small k. A subsequent book chapter (Springer, 2024) revisits these problems but does not present a closed-form solution, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems Regarding the Number of Lines and Slopes in Arrangements that Determine Shapes
status_evidence.snippet: empirical evidence is reported for small numbers of k offering partial answers to the three problems above

status_evidence.title: Arrangements Containing Shapes: Mathematical Features and Their Use in Visual Calculating
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses triples (k,n,d) of registration marks, construction lines, and distinct slopes in arrangements.
status_evidence.claim: Follow-up work studies the same triples without providing a closed-form answer.
